title: False Signal
hook: Two callers claim the same identity. Choose which evidence to request, compare their accounts with the line log, and decide whose door to unlock.
audience: Players who enjoy short deduction thrillers, analog interfaces and consequential decisions from incomplete but fair evidence.
core_loop: Receive a suspicious call; inspect its recording and route log; choose one of two questions; make an evidence-based routing decision; see a brief consequence; carry one consequence flag into the next call.
working_title_note: Working name; no name or trademark clearance established.
evidence_limits: Desk research only. No competitor hands-on session, own playable build, target-player interview, fun validation or purchase-intent measurement. Historical topic growth is distinct from a verified current trend phase.
commercial_hypothesis: Offline premium Windows microgame. USD 3.99-4.99 is the initial question for six substantial calls and a complete compact story. USD 9.99 is the owner ceiling, conditional on genre/price evidence and achievable worthwhile scope; this proposal does not yet justify that price.

cash_assumptions.note: Planning inputs only, no spending authorized. Existing machine/tools assumed; subscription/compute costs not measured. Steam fee and any applicable store tax separate from optional assets.

calendar_note: Build estimates include the prototype, final-direction art/audio, finite content, save/settings, packaged Windows QA and draft store media. Steam onboarding/review/waiting and recruitment are separate; no launch date committed.
support_estimate: Reserve 1–2 owner hours around launch for triage/review, with agent implementation as needed; actual demand and defect burden unknown.

decision_history.reason: Research recommendation only; owner has not selected a game or authorized a prototype.

Third recommended experiment in the wider slate for a contrasting short thriller with a clear authentication choice. Current trend timing, writing/audio quality and value of six cases remain substantial uncertainties; no selection.

score_notes.demand: Short low-price horror has strong purchaser response through The Exit 8 and The Cabin Factory. Home Safety Hotline and DEAD LETTER DEPT. are closer desk-horror references but USD 14.99, above ceiling; Telephone Call is a low-response counterexample. No direct paid-unit evidence for our exact phone-deduction format.
score_notes.distinctiveness: Caller authentication, limited questions and persistent evidence differ from matching household hazards to a database, but phone horror is crowded.
score_notes.fun_potential: Fair evidence choices could sustain tension, but no test shows this avoids rote checklists.
score_notes.scope_fit: Even six substantial calls require clear writing, audio, captions and clue QA; 5–7 days is conditional and riskier than the craft candidates.
score_notes.distribution: A contradictory pair of callers is an understandable trailer premise. Searchers seeking an AI security tool may have no interest in fiction.

inspiration.topic: AI voice authenticity and concern about manipulated media
inspiration.connection: The player tests a caller's claimed identity through consistent evidence; the uncertainty is the game activity.
inspiration.why_phase_unverified: Exploding Topics' public topic displays +24% across a two-year selector; other articles use different terms/periods. They are one provider and no current series was exported.
inspiration.evergreen_promise: A finite, fair deduction thriller works as a story about impostors even after AI headlines cool. No continuing news feed is needed.
inspiration.searchable_name: Optional. The product should clearly be described as a fictional game, not sold as a working voice detector.

evidence.claim: The public topic page displays a two-year selector, +24% growth and 3.6K volume, accessed September 6. Exact geographic coverage, monthly curve and seasonal adjustment were unavailable. This is provider-reported interest in a tool-related query.

The August 24, 2026 US list includes AI voice detection. Its +3,200% headline uses an unspecified comparison horizon, so that percentage is not used to claim current acceleration or combined with the topic page.

Home Safety Hotline sells telephone-based deduction through a catalog. The saved snapshot has 2,754 all-language Steam-purchase reviews, 2,494 positive, at USD 14.99; it is an audience reference with substantially broader content.
The developer advertises typing-based horror with rich audio and roughly 120-minute runs, illustrating the writing and sound expectations of this adjacent audience.

Nightmare Collection: Telephone Call is a paid short phone-horror comparable. The saved API snapshot has 17 Steam-purchase reviews, 7 positive, at USD 2.99. A telephone and horror theme alone do not establish appeal.

Unknown Number's developer advertises microphone-controlled phone calls and hardware requirements; the saved snapshot has only 18 Steam-purchase reviews. We avoid adding voice-input compatibility work.

One sampled positive Home Safety Hotline review likes follow-up calls after errors but finds repeat play less compelling once scenarios are known. This is an anecdote from a small purposive sample, not a prevalence estimate.

One sampled negative Home Safety Hotline review finds repeated call-to-database matching dull. This motivates testing information choices before adding story content, not a claim about the average player.
The Cabin Factory: USD 2.99 regular / 2.09 current, 3,435 all-language Steam-purchase reviews, 90.9% positive. Short-horror price-format reference, not same mechanic.
The Exit 8: USD 3.99 regular / 2.79 current, 10,874 reviews, 93.0% positive. Short-horror reference in the allowed price band.

Publisher describes The Exit 8 as having sold over one million copies on PC and Switch. Platform 8 page discusses its November 2024 console release; exact disclosure publication date unavailable. Not Steam-only sales.

May 30, 2026 developer post reports about 1,000 Steam copies of What's the Password? in its first 48 hours at USD 7.99 regular / 6.95 launch offer, with some additional bundle discounts. Adjacent deduction evidence, not phone-horror or few-day production proof.

prototype_envelope.scope: One desk, three calls, two clue rules, one meaningful question choice, captions and at least one exchange with finished-direction audio.

production_envelope.scope: One shift of six substantial calls, three explicit clue rules, maximum two question choices per case, one persistent consequence flag, one ending with brief outcome variations; fixed recordings and complete clue-equivalent captions.
production_envelope.owner_note: Includes fairness/story/audio review. Revisions to clue logic can push beyond the allowance.

risks: The weakest trend link in this shortlist: tool searches may have little overlap with players seeking fiction, and current growth phase is unknown.
Phone-operator horror has close competitors; insufficient meaningful decisions would make this a derivative checklist.
Branching and voiced content can expand rapidly; an independent challenge cut the initial twelve cases to six.
A twist must not invalidate taught evidence rules; every decisive clue needs caption parity.
Six calls is a scope cap, not a promised duration or price justification. Writing and sound quality must be demonstrated early.
next_test: If chosen, test a one-day three-call slice with one finished-direction audio exchange. With five available players, continue if 4/5 explain decisive evidence, 3/5 choose a question for an information reason and 3/5 request another case. Log every wrong answer defensible from the supplied evidence and fix ambiguity before adding cases. Hold if tension needs unfair surprises or the questions are rote.
independent_challenge: The market-analyst challenged topic-to-audience transfer and rejected the original twelve-case/three-shift budget. Adopted six-call cap, one consequence flag, fixed recordings and clue-equivalent captions. No independent playtest occurred.
decision_reason: Third recommended experiment in the wider slate for a contrasting short thriller with a clear authentication choice. Current trend timing, writing/audio quality and value of six cases remain substantial uncertainties; no selection.
